title: metrics.py: compare_metrics treats missing latency as 0 us
description:
## Problem

Metrics.snapshot() always emits latency_us with min/max/mean/p50/p95/p99. When _latency_count == 0 those fields are None.

compare_metrics, for each latency key:

  if b_val is None and v_val is None: continue
  b_val = float(b_val) if b_val is not None else 0.0
  v_val = float(v_val) if v_val is not None else 0.0

A baseline with no deliveries (None) vs a variant that delivers at 100 µs becomes 0 → 100. _is_significant(0, 100) is True for counts, _rate_direction marks every latency_* as degraded (lower-is-better). Six degraded latency metrics outweigh transmissions/receptions/delivery_rate improvements, so overall_verdict is "worse".

A/B oracles then prefer a silent run over a run that actually delivers. 9098.37 fixed rate 0→0.9 significance; it did not change this None→0 mapping. test_compare_zero_baseline and test_compare_missing_latency use hand-built dicts without latency_us, so they never see snapshot() output.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py (compare_metrics latency block, snapshot, latency_stats)
- python/tests/sim/test_metrics.py (test_compare_zero_baseline, test_compare_missing_latency)
close_reason: Duplicate of project-LICHEN-worker6-9098.45 (compare_metrics None latency → 0; same root cause, opposite A/B direction already covered by skip-either-None design).
